summary: Dedicated pool throughput collapse during staggered prefetch wave causing GPU starvation
description:
Issue summary: Customer (ScribeLabs) reports large p99/p95 latency increases and an overall throughput collapse for requests routed to their dedicated GPU pool starting 2026-03-10 07:30 UTC. Impact: production traffic for several customer routes degraded to <10% expected throughput for ~40 minutes, causing user-facing timeouts. Environment: prod dedicated pool in eu-west serving mixed chat and classification workloads on pinned model redwood-chat-3b-v2. Observed symptoms include repeated GPU allocation failures, batch queue pileups, and autoscaler failing to scale up fast enough.

High-level hypothesis: a staggered prefetch sweep from multiple internal tenants created transient NVMe I/O pressure and prefetched large KV caches which forced the allocator to serialize GPU attachments; combined with the autoscaler's cooldown heuristics this produced a window where new allocations were throttled, leading to noisy-neighbor-like starvation in the dedicated pool.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Route sustained short-chat streams (~200-300ms per request) plus intermittent long-context classification jobs to a dedicated pool pinned to redwood-chat-3b-v2.
2) Trigger a prefetch/config-sweep across multiple tenants in the same pool by deploying a policy change (simulated via internal tooling).
3) Observe allocator logs and GPU attach timings and measure per-tenant batch queue depth and p99 latency over a 30-60 minute window.
4) Confirm autoscaler does not immediately add capacity due to backoff/cooldown.

Expected behavior: smooth autoscale ramp and bounded p99 latency. Observed: bursty attach failures and throughput collapse until a manual override/increase is applied.

investigation_notes: 07:33 UTC: replicated slot-attach latencies correlate with elevated NVMe IO wait on nodes in eu-west cluster N-12.
07:38 UTC: prefetcher telemetry shows overlapping cache population jobs from 5 tenants; two tenants launched large context prefetches within a 2-minute window.
07:40 UTC: autoscaler logs indicate cooldown prevented immediate scale-up; cooldown policy requisition did not consider nvme-io as a trigger metric.
07:45 UTC: manual scaling (add 2 gpus) brought throughput back to baseline in ~5 minutes, indicating capacity rather than model failure.

Hypothesis: combination of storage I/O saturation and conservative autoscaler cooldown created a transient allocation bottleneck; tenant prefetch waves acted as noisy neighbor events despite dedicated pool tenancy due to shared node-level IO subsystems.
Telemetry sliced by tenant shows ScribeLabs' requests were getting queued behind a small number of prefetch-heavy sessions from internal test tenants.
Potential mitigations: introduce nvme_io pressure metric into autoscaler triggers; stagger prefetch jobs; implement per-node I/O fairness (limit concurrent large prefetches).
comments: Customer comment (2026-03-10 08:05 UTC) - Helena @ ScribeLabs: "We saw user sessions timeout and a spike in errors across two routes. Appreciate any ETA, this is impacting onboarding demos."
Support (2026-03-10 08:18 UTC) - Aisha: "Acknowledged, we're investigating. Can you confirm if any large batch jobs started around 07:20-07:40 UTC on your side?"
Customer (2026-03-10 08:22 UTC) - Helena: "No large jobs on our side; most traffic was short chat. We did roll a small model-pin change earlier but that shouldn't trigger heavy prefetch."

SRE (2026-03-10 09:02 UTC) - Miguel: "Found concurrent prefetch sweeps from internal QA tenants; starting manual scale and isolating those sessions. Pushing patch to autoscaler logic to consider nvme_io."
Support (2026-03-10 10:10 UTC) - Aisha: "Manual mitigation complete, we've added temporary capacity to ScribeLabs' pool and paused QA prefetch jobs. Monitoring for stability."
resolution: Workaround applied: manually added 2 GPUs to ScribeLabs' dedicated pool and paused overlapping prefetch jobs from internal tenants, which restored throughput. Root cause: node-level NVMe I/O saturation from concurrent prefetch sweeps combined with autoscaler cooldown prevented timely scale-up and serialized GPU attachments. Permanent fixes planned: (1) autoscaler change to include nvme_io and queue_depth as up-scaling triggers, (2) a prefetch-scheduling gate to stagger large cache population jobs across nodes, (3) implement per-node I/O throttles for prefetcher to avoid blocking attach paths. Follow-ups: scheduled postmortem with SRE and Runtime teams (CON-2026-03-PM-72) and a customer-facing RCA by 2026-03-15.
next_steps: PR to autoscaler: add nvme_io and batch_queue_depth thresholds for aggressive up-scaling (owner: autoscaler team) - target merge 2026-03-12
Implement prefetch gate in prefetcher service to avoid simultaneous large cache jobs on same node (owner: runtime team) - ETA 2026-03-18
Create runbook entry for dedicated pools to detect nvme_io-pressure and manual scale runbook (owner: support) - ETA 2026-03-13
customer_impact_note: ScribeLabs experienced a 40-minute production degradation during peak onboarding period affecting new user sign-ups and demos. No data loss, only increased error and timeout rates. Customer requested an RCA and timeline for permanent mitigation.
